findings.title: Untimed deltas dropped by run window
findings.problem: kimi.metrics-processor.ts:216 and opencode.metrics-processor.ts:393-394 substitute Date.now() when a step/message lacks a timestamp. With the new run window, that synthetic 'now' is judged against the upper bound (next record's startTime) instead of being kept as untimed, which MetricsWriter otherwise does for non-finite times.
findings.impact: In a wrapper/daemon pass over a transcript shared with a later record, every untimed kimi step or opencode message is dropped as after_end and its tokens/tools are never reported for any record. Reachability unconfirmed: depends on how often transcripts omit event.time / time.created.
findings.recommendation: Stop substituting Date.now() for a missing event time: use NaN (kimi.metrics-processor.ts:216 `typeof event.time === 'number' ? event.time : NaN`; opencode.metrics-processor.ts:393-394 return NaN) so MetricsWriter keeps the delta as untimed instead of judging a synthetic 'now' against the upper bound. Check downstream consumers tolerate a non-finite timestamp.

findings.title: Hook processing context omits hookProcess and bounds
findings.problem: Regression gap: performIncrementalSync builds its ProcessingContext via buildProcessingContext and only adds recordsBeforeMs; it never sets hookProcess, abortSignal or syncDeadlineMs (only delivery.ts:157-163 sets them, on the sync context). resolveRunWindow (run-window.ts:22) and lockBoundsOf therefore treat `codemie hook` as a wrapper: they run the nextRecordStart scan hook.ts:314-315 deliberately skips, and lock waits ignore the hook's deadline/abort and pid-only liveness. Every window test hands processors a hand-built { hookProcess: true } context, so no test catches it.
findings.impact: Consumer: Stop and SessionEnd hooks via performIncrementalSync -> sessionAdapter.processSession -> every metrics/conversation processor. Contrary to the PR's stated contract, a hook applies a later-record upper bound (dropping deltas as after_end) and a held metrics/conversation lock can block the hook for the full 10 s budget past its deadline/abort.
findings.recommendation: In performIncrementalSync (or buildProcessingContext), set context.hookProcess, context.abortSignal and context.syncDeadlineMs from the hook's options (as delivery.ts:157-163 does for the sync context), and add a test that drives performIncrementalSync/handleSessionEnd with hookProcess=true and asserts the context handed to processSession carries them.

findings.title: Wall-clock perf assertion in writer test
findings.problem: The test 'appends one delta to a 20 000-line file quickly' asserts performance.now() delta < 100 ms, while appendDeltas reads every recordId in the file under a pid-lock.
findings.impact: Timing-dependent assertion on loaded CI runners makes the suite flaky and can block unrelated merges. Reachability of the flake on CI unconfirmed.
findings.recommendation: Replace the <100 ms wall-clock assertion with a deterministic check (e.g. assert the file is not rewritten / bytes appended only), or widen the bound generously so CI load cannot fail it.

findings.title: Commit headers exceed commitlint 100-char limit
findings.problem: git-workflow.md requires Conventional Commits enforced by commitlint.config.cjs, which extends @commitlint/config-conventional (header-max-length 100, error level). Headers of 997f8856 (116 chars) and 07cc00e0 (107 chars) exceed it.
findings.impact: The commit-msg hook would reject these headers, so they either bypassed the hook or will fail commitlint in CI or on rebase, blocking the workflow.
findings.recommendation: Shorten the headers of 997f8856 (116 chars) and 07cc00e0 (107 chars) to 100 chars or fewer, moving the second clause into the body, or ensure the squash-merge PR title is 100 chars or fewer.
